title: Vault content has NO separate permission level from evidence-management — verified as a real gap, not just a suspicion
description: The task premise ('vault items have separate permission levels from standard evidence-management') does not hold: src/config/permissions.js's MODULES/NAV_MODULES arrays contain no 'compliance_vault' entry at all. Every route that could plausibly back a compliance-vault UI (evidence.routes.js) is gated exclusively by 'evidence.read'/'evidence.update'/'evidence.delete'. This test guards against a future implementation accidentally introducing a compliance_vault.* permission that is checked nowhere, or worse, granting compliance-vault access via evidence.* while believing it is a separate, narrower grant.
preconditions: A role with 'evidence.read' but explicitly no other GRC module permissions
steps: Assign a user a role with only 'evidence.read'
As that user, request every endpoint that would plausibly serve compliance-vault content (GET /api/evidence, GET /api/evidence/organization/:orgId, GET /api/evidence/:evidenceId)
Confirm each succeeds solely on the strength of 'evidence.read'
expectedResult: All requests succeed under 'evidence.read' alone — confirming there is no additional, narrower 'vault' permission gate a security reviewer might mistakenly assume exists. Document this as a real finding: access control for compliance-vault content is entirely inherited from evidence-management, with zero independent enforcement layer.

title: Role/permission update endpoint rejects an attempt to grant a fabricated 'compliance_vault.read' or 'compliance_vault.admin' permission string
description: Regression guard: if a role-management UI or API ever accepts arbitrary permission strings without validating against isValidPermission(), an admin (or a compromised admin session) could persist a meaningless 'compliance_vault.admin' grant that looks authoritative in an audit but enforces nothing anywhere, creating a false sense of least-privilege.
preconditions: Logged in as org admin with role.update permission
expectedResult: Request is rejected (400) citing an invalid/unrecognized permission string — the backend's isValidPermission() check must reject 'compliance_vault.*' since it is not in MODULES or EXTRA_VALID_PERMISSIONS.

title: Cross-org access to evidence backing compliance-vault content is blocked identically to the evidence-management endpoint (no vault-specific bypass path)
description: Because compliance-vault has no dedicated backend routes, this is a regression guard mirroring EVID-SEC-001: confirms there is no shadow/legacy route (e.g. /api/compliance-vault/*, /api/vault/evidence/*) that duplicates evidence retrieval logic without the same augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant + requireProjectMembership + org-scoping middleware chain applied in evidence.routes.js.
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B), each with an evidence item of type 'certificate'
Valid JWT for a user in org A
steps: As an org A user, probe for any route matching /api/compliance-vault/*, /api/vault/*, /api/evidence-vault/* on the backend
If any such route exists, attempt GET against org B's evidence ID through it
expectedResult: No such route exists (404 on all probes) — all evidence data, including certificate-type items a vault UI would surface, is served exclusively through the existing evidence.routes.js endpoints, which already enforce org/project scoping. There is no parallel, less-guarded surface.

title: A user removed from a project immediately loses access to previously-viewed vault file attachments
description: evidence.routes.js:55-56 gates GET /:evidenceId/files/:fileId/download-url and /content behind requirePermission('evidence.read') plus requireProjectMembership() via augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant(getEvidenceProjectId). Since a compliance-vault detail view would call the same endpoints for its 'file attachments' section, a stale client-side cache of a previously-generated presigned URL must not remain the only access control — the endpoint itself must re-check membership on every call.
preconditions: User B was a member of Project X and viewed an evidence file's attachments
User B is then removed from Project X
steps: As User B, call GET /:evidenceId/files/:fileId/download-url for a file in Project X after removal
As User B, attempt to reuse a previously-obtained presigned S3 URL directly against S3
expectedResult: The download-url endpoint call returns 403 post-removal. Any already-issued presigned URL is short-lived and expires independently, but the application-level endpoint must not re-issue new URLs to the removed user.

title: No evidence/compliance-vault API response ever leaks VAULT_ADDRESS, VAULT_CP_WRITE_ROLE_ID, or a HashiCorp Vault client_token
description: vault.service.js manages a completely separate HashiCorp Vault instance (AppRole login, KV v2 secrets) for cloud-posture provider credentials — unrelated to the compliance-vault GRC feature. The shared word 'vault' creates a real risk that a future developer or an error-message leak conflates the two, e.g. an unhandled exception in evidence upload accidentally surfacing a Vault client_token in a stack trace returned to the client.
steps: Trigger a 500 error in any evidence/*, evidence-upload/*, or evidence-mapping/* endpoint (e.g. malformed payload causing an unhandled exception)
Inspect the full error response body and any server logs correlated to the request
expectedResult: No response body or log line reachable by the client contains VAULT_ADDRESS, VAULT_CP_WRITE_ROLE_ID, VAULT_CP_WRITE_SECRET_ID, or a raw Vault client_token — the two 'vault' systems remain fully isolated even under error conditions.

title: A user without evidence.read cannot infer vault item existence from the confidentialityLevel field via error message differences
description: evidence.model.js's metadata.confidentialityLevel enum ('public','internal','confidential','restricted','top_secret') suggests differentiated access is intended for sensitive vault documents, but evidence.routes.js applies a single flat 'evidence.read' gate with no per-confidentiality-level check. Verifies the API does not leak whether a 'restricted'/'top_secret' item exists via a distinguishable 403 vs 404 response to an unauthorized caller.
preconditions: An evidence item exists with metadata.confidentialityLevel = 'top_secret' in a project the caller is not a member of
steps: As a user with no membership in the item's project, call GET /api/evidence/:evidenceId for the top_secret item
Repeat for a random non-existent evidenceId
Compare response status codes and bodies
expectedResult: Both cases return an identical, non-distinguishing response (403 or 404 consistently) — the confidentialityLevel field has no dedicated enforcement path today, so at minimum existence must not be leaked through response variance; flag if confidentialityLevel is found to have zero server-side enforcement anywhere, since that field would then be decorative metadata only.
